notation.meaning: graph with node set \(V\)
degree of \(v\) within the subgraph induced by \(S\); for a directed graph the in-, out- or total degree as chosen
the \(k\)-core: the maximal induced subgraph in which every node has \(\deg\ge k\)
core number: the largest \(k\) with \(v\in H_k\)

formulas.name: Core number (Seidman 1983)
formulas.latex: c(v)=\max\{k: v\in H_k\},\qquad H_k=\text{the largest }S\text{ with }\min_{u\in S}\deg_S(u)\ge k
formulas.where: Every graph has a unique \(k\)-core for each \(k\), possibly empty. Computed in \(O(m)\) by repeated removal of the minimum-degree node (Batagelj and Zaversnik 2003). The definition is for simple graphs; counting loops and parallel edges in the degree is a convention.

formulas.name: Core subsets
formulas.where: The \(k\)-shell, \(k\)-crust and \(k\)-corona derived from core numbers; \(k\)-core = \(\{v:c(v)\ge k\}\).

variants.coreness: The core number \(c(v)\) of every node; for directed graphs the degree in the peeling is the in-, out- or in-plus-out degree.
variants.core_subset: A node subset derived from the core numbers: the \(k\)-core, \(k\)-shell, \(k\)-crust or \(k\)-corona (with default \(k\) the maximum core number for the core and shell).
variants.cat_core_decomposition_sequence: Documented for NetworKit as the core decomposition sequence; not recorded in detail.

formulas.name: Onion decomposition (Hebert-Dufresne et al. 2016)
formulas.latex: \text{repeat: }k\leftarrow\max\bigl(k,\min_{u\in R}\deg_R(u)\bigr);\ L=\{v\in R:\deg_R(v)\le k\};\ \ell(v)=\text{round index for }v\in L;\ R\leftarrow R\setminus L
formulas.where: A refinement of the core decomposition that records, for each node, the round in which it is peeled when all nodes of degree at most the current core number \(k\) are removed simultaneously. The core number of a node is the value of \(k\) at its removal; layers are ordered from 1.

1 if \(i,j\) are tied, else 0
a partition into \(k\) groups

formulas.name: Factions error count
formulas.where: Ties between groups plus missing ties within groups: the deviations from the ideal pattern of complete groups with no ties between them. The best partition minimizes \(E\) for the given \(k\); found by a heuristic search, so not guaranteed optimal and not unique.

variants.cat_factions: The factions partition as documented for UCINET; the options are not recorded.
variants.factions_errors: The partition into \(k\) groups with the fewest errors \(E(p)\) against the ideal pattern of ties inside groups only, by tabu search from random starts.

edge_cases.definition_gives: With \(k>n\) groups some groups are empty and cannot reduce \(E\).
Within-group missing ties are the only errors; the best partition puts each node alone (\(E=0\)) when \(k\ge n\).
One group (\(E=0\)); with \(k\) groups forced non-empty, ties between groups are errors.
Several partitions may reach the minimum; the search returns one.
\(k\) must be between 1 and \(n\).

formulas.name: k-plex (Seidman and Foster 1978)
formulas.where: Each member is adjacent to all but at most \(k-1\) of the other members; a 1-plex is a clique. Maximal \(k\)-plexes cannot be extended. Defined for \(k\ge1\); sets of fewer than \(k\) nodes satisfy it trivially, so a minimum size is imposed in practice.

variants.k_plexes: All maximal \(k\)-plexes of at least a given size.

edge_cases.definition_gives: No node set.
Any set of at most \(k\) nodes is a \(k\)-plex.
Sets smaller than the minimum size are not reported.
The whole node set is a 1-plex.
\(k<1\) is meaningless (a node would need more than all other members as neighbours).

notation.meaning: simple undirected graph (direction ignored, parallel edges merged, loops dropped) with node set \(V\), \(n=|V|\)
edge connectivity between \(u\) and \(v\): the minimum number of edges whose removal disconnects them, equal to the maximum number of edge-disjoint \(u\)-\(v\) paths

formulas.name: Lambda connectivity (Borgatti, Everett and Shirey 1990)
formulas.latex: \lambda(u,v)=\min\{|F|:F\subseteq E,\ u,v\text{ in different components of }(V,E\setminus F)\}
formulas.where: Menger's theorem equates it with the maximum number of edge-disjoint paths; computed for all pairs from the \(n-1\) maximum flows of Gusfield's equivalent flow tree (Gusfield 1990), \(\lambda(u,v)\) being the minimum edge value on the tree path. Defined for \(u\ne v\); 0 for nodes in different components.

variants.lambda_connectivity: The matrix \(\lambda(u,v)\) over all pairs of the simple undirected graph (read off the flow tree).

formulas.name: Lambda set (Borgatti, Everett and Shirey 1990)
formulas.latex: S\ \text{is a lambda set}\iff \min_{i\ne j\in S}\lambda(i,j)>\max_{i\in S,\,k\notin S}\lambda(i,k)
formulas.where: A set that is more connected internally than to any outside node.
